walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Ieper' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140005)
walls.note: Ypres: Burgundian stone wall finished 1409, with bastions in front of the gates from the late 16th c.; Vauban's great works are later (1680s). The ring follows the moats and ramparts that survive in OSM (east and south) and the line of the Ieperlee (west); it matches the inner rampart on the Ferraris map (1777) within about 50 m.

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall of c. 1200-1304, one of the largest secular Gothic buildings of Europe, with its belfry; intact in 1650 (destroyed in 1914-18 and rebuilt). The Kattenstoet - cats thrown from the belfry - is an old Lent custom here (start and 1650 practice not verified).
Cathedral of the bishopric of Ypres (1559-1801); Bishop Cornelius Jansenius (d. 1638) is buried here.
Parish church in the south of the town.
